title: Angular Momentum, Moment of Inertia & Circular Motion

questions.question: Uniform circular motion is motion along a circle with constant:
questions.explanation: In uniform circular motion, the speed remains constant while the direction of velocity changes continuously.

questions.question: In uniform circular motion, the velocity changes because its:
questions.explanation: Velocity is a vector. In uniform circular motion the speed is constant, but the direction changes, so velocity changes.

questions.question: The velocity of a body in circular motion is directed:
questions.explanation: Instantaneous velocity in circular motion is always tangent to the circular path.

questions.question: Angular displacement is usually measured in:
questions.explanation: Angular displacement is an angle and is usually measured in radians.

questions.question: One complete revolution corresponds to an angle of:
questions.explanation: One complete revolution is 360°, which equals 2π radians.

questions.question: Angular velocity is the rate of change of:
questions.explanation: Angular velocity ω is the rate of change of angular displacement: ω = Δθ/Δt.

questions.question: The SI unit of angular velocity is:
questions.explanation: Angular velocity is measured in radians per second (rad/s).

questions.question: The period of circular motion is the time taken for:
questions.explanation: The period T is the time taken to complete one full revolution.

questions.question: Frequency is the number of revolutions per:
questions.explanation: Frequency f is the number of revolutions completed per unit time.

questions.question: Period and frequency are:
questions.explanation: Period and frequency are related by f = 1/T, so they are reciprocals.

questions.question: The SI unit of frequency is the:
questions.explanation: The SI unit of frequency is the hertz (Hz), equal to one cycle per second.

questions.question: The linear speed of a body in circular motion is related to its angular velocity and the:
questions.explanation: Linear speed is v = rω, so it depends on angular velocity and radius.

questions.question: At a given angular velocity, a point farther from the axis has a linear speed that is:
questions.explanation: Since v = rω, for the same ω a larger radius gives a greater linear speed.

questions.question: Centripetal acceleration is directed:
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration points towards the centre of the circular path.

questions.question: The work done by the centripetal force on a body in uniform circular motion is:
questions.explanation: Centripetal force is perpendicular to the displacement, so the work done is zero.

questions.question: For a stone whirled on a string, the centripetal force is provided by the:
questions.explanation: The tension in the string provides the inward centripetal force on the stone.

questions.question: For the Moon orbiting Earth, the centripetal force is provided by:
questions.explanation: The Moon is kept in orbit by Earth’s gravitational pull, which provides the centripetal force.

questions.question: A body moving in a vertical circle has a tension in the string that is greatest at the:
questions.explanation: At the bottom of a vertical circle, tension must support the weight and provide centripetal force, so it is greatest there.

questions.question: Kepler’s second law states that a planet sweeps out:
questions.explanation: Kepler’s second law: a planet sweeps out equal areas in equal times.

questions.question: According to Kepler’s second law, a planet moves fastest when it is:
questions.explanation: A planet moves fastest when it is closest to the Sun, where its orbital radius is smallest.

questions.question: Newton’s law of gravitation states that every two masses attract each other with a force proportional to the:
questions.explanation: Newton’s law of gravitation: F ∝ m₁m₂/r², so the force is proportional to the product of the masses.

questions.question: The gravitational force between two masses is always:
questions.explanation: Gravitational force is always attractive between two masses.

questions.question: The constant G in Newton’s law is called the:
questions.explanation: The constant G is the universal gravitational constant.

questions.question: The constant G was first measured experimentally by:
questions.explanation: The value of G was first measured experimentally by Henry Cavendish using a torsion balance.

questions.question: Gravitational force pairs between two bodies are:
options: Equal in magnitude and same direction
questions.explanation: By Newton’s third law, gravitational force pairs are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.

questions.question: The acceleration due to gravity at Earth’s surface depends on Earth’s mass and:
questions.explanation: At Earth’s surface, g = GM/R², so it depends on Earth’s mass and Earth’s radius, not on the falling body’s mass.

questions.question: The acceleration due to gravity with increasing height above Earth’s surface:
questions.explanation: Since g = GM/r², as height increases r increases, so g decreases.

questions.question: The gravitational field strength at a point is the force per unit:
questions.explanation: Gravitational field strength is the gravitational force per unit mass: g = F/m.

questions.question: Escape velocity is the minimum speed needed for a body to:
options: Orbit Earth at a low height
Reach the top of a building
questions.explanation: Escape velocity is the minimum speed required to leave a planet’s gravitational field without further propulsion.

questions.question: A geostationary satellite has an orbital period equal to Earth’s:
questions.explanation: A geostationary satellite orbits with a period equal to Earth’s rotation period, so it stays above the same point on the equator.
